title: Beyond Algorithm Evolution: An LLM-Driven Framework for the Co-Evolution of Swarm Intelligence Optimization Algorithms and Prompts

mechanism.domainTask: Co-evolution of swarm-intelligence optimization algorithms and prompts
mechanism.populationDetail: The framework selects among multiple candidate algorithms in one pool; no island partition or maintained search tree is described.
mechanism.archiveDetail: No separate elite archive is specified; retaining top-performing algorithms is discussed as a possible greedy update strategy.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The paper gives a generic top-performing retention strategy but does not fully specify the implemented algorithm-pool survivor/update rule.
mechanism.generationDetail: Mutation locally replaces one operator in one parent algorithm, while crossover combines operator content from two parent algorithms.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: The candidate's scalar task score and source code condition later generation and contribute to prompt-template performance assessment.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Mutation selects one algorithm; crossover selects two. The paper describes rank-based probability or greedy parent selection without fixing one universal rule.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: Coupled co-evolution of algorithm candidates and distinct mutation/crossover prompt-template pools, where prompt utility is measured by downstream algorithm performance change.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/Beyond Algorithm Evolution An LLM-Driven Framework for the Co-Evolution of Swarm Intelligence Optimization Algorithms and Prompts.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Replacement/update details are generic; generation-operator selection is not specified; multi-model count reflects separate experimental backbones rather than within-run collaboration. Do not code generic parallel/time-constrained evaluation suggestions as implemented procedure.
